sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Indian Archaeology 1957 to 1958, Navdatoli and Ujjain
sources.note: Printed pp. 32 and 36, indexed original. Navdatoli grain sample is explicitly earlier Chalcolithic material, not a fifth-century Avanti menu. Ujjain Period II conventionally circa 500 to 200 BCE.

sources.title: Vimala S. Begley, Penn Museum: The Ganga-Yamuna Basin (1966)
sources.note: Direct full original read, passages about Ujjain buildings, tank and workshops, after the circa 500 to 200 BCE phase discussion. Historical archaeological synthesis; avoid obsolete pan-Indian earliest-iron claim.

sources.title: Udana 5.6: Sona, translated by Thanissaro Bhikkhu
sources.note: Full primary translation checked. Literary representation of Buddha-era Avanti, not contemporary written field notes.

sources.title: Vinaya, Mahavagga V.13: Avanti and the Southern Route
sources.note: Direct Pali/English table, V.13.6 and V.13.13. Group cumulatively with existing Magadha Mahavagga material and medical chapter.

sources.title: Vinaya, Mahavagga VIII.1.23 to 26: King Pajjota and Jivaka
sources.note: Indexed original Pali/English passage checked; royal jaundice and disguised ghee are a Buddhist literary story, not clinical evidence. Same underlying Mahavagga work as bathing and existing Magadha references.

sources.title: John Marshall, Alfred Foucher and N. G. Majumdar: The Monuments of Sanchi, volume I
sources.note: Indexed original pp. 278 and 307 checked; inscription 76, plate 129.64, Luders 221. Modern scholarly Roman transliteration of Brahmi. No invented Unicode Brahmi. p278 dates early votives to second/first centuries BCE.

Existing Magadha and Maurya cards stay separate; no alias to later Malwa/Ujjain dynasties. Archaeological phases wider than atlas span are made public.
